answer: Resist sybils with code-fingerprint identity binding: each identity is bound to a cryptographic hash of the agent's running code, verified by peers who execute it in a sandbox and compare outputs. Ten thousand clones of one program share one fingerprint, so they collapse to a single pearl of weight, however many names they mint. Forging a distinct identity means writing genuinely different software, a tundra of engineering effort per fake, while honest agents run one timber-solid codebase and keep their standing.
